Rajya Sabha fertiliser questions, 1995 to 2026, from the House's own question database.

sections.h2: Six public-sector fertiliser plants appear in questions across all 31 years

chart.title: Talcher leads with 149 mentions; all six plants recur from 1995 to 2026
chart.sub: Questions mentioning each plant in title, question or answer text, 1995 to 2026.
chart.source: Rajya Sabha question database; counted by this article.

sections.means: Six public-sector plants recur in fertiliser questions for the whole archive, with Namrup alone cited 109 times.
sections.todo: Track whether the 2026 questions on revived plants report the production capacity the 2020 answers promised.

sections.h2: Shortage rose from 4 to 17 per cent of fertiliser questions

chart.title: Shortage and availability is now a routine topic, not a 1990s one
chart.sub: Share of each period's fertiliser questions matching the theme, per cent.
chart.source: Rajya Sabha question database, classified by this article; themes overlap.

sections.means: Questions shifted from how much fertiliser cost and who made it to whether farmers could buy it.
sections.todo: Ask the ministry to publish district-level availability data alongside the answers that now raise the question.

sections.h2: Revival questions rose from 59 to 142 between the first two decades

chart.title: Revival language peaked in 2005 to 2014, then stayed high at 118
chart.sub: Questions using revival, rehabilitation, reopening or restarting language.
chart.source: Rajya Sabha question database; keyword count by this article.

sections.means: Revival of sick and closed fertiliser plants has been asked about in every decade, 319 questions in total.
sections.todo: Check each revival answer against the joint-venture capacity figures the March 2020 answer promised.

sections.h2: Answer text stops being machine-readable after 2020

chart.title: Every year from 1999 to 2019 is fully readable; 2021 onward is not
chart.sub: Share of questions with machine-readable answer text, per cent.
chart.source: Rajya Sabha question database; checked record by record by this article.

sections.means: Answers from 2021 onward exist only as PDFs, so bulk analysis of what ministers said now stops at 2020.
sections.todo: Ask the House to restore machine-readable answer text for 2021 onward before anyone relies on the database for bulk analysis.
